newsitem.title: USA: U.S.Can sees Q2 earnings hurt, CEO to leave.
newsitem.headline: U.S.Can sees Q2 earnings hurt, CEO to leave.

text.p: U.S. Can Corp, announcing a major restructuring, said Wednesday that second quarter earnings would be hurt by various factors and that it had hired Salomon Brothers Inc to assist it in evaluating strategic alternatives.
The manufacturer of steel and plastic containers also said William Smith would retire as chairman, president and chief executive officer effective June 30, 1998.
Company directors have begun a search for a successor to Smith, who will remain a director of U.S. Can after his retirement.

U.S. Can said an extremely competitive pricing environment, steel cost increases and lower aerosol volumes will have an adverse effect on its second quarter results. In the 1996 second quarter the company earned $5.1 million, or $0.39 a share, on sales of $180.6 million.
U.S. Can's restructuring plan is aimed at making the company more efficient. The actions include closing several plants, affecting more than 300 employees, and taking charges of $30-$35 million.
